# Behavioral Specification: Unbuffered OTP Partition Controller

## 1. Purpose

The unbuffered OTP partition controller provides read access to a single OTP partition. It is called “unbuffered” because data is not held in a local shadow copy; every enabled read is serviced directly from the OTP interface.

The controller also loads and holds the partition digest, reports access and error status, and provides effective read/write lock indications for the partition.

## 2. Reset and Power-Up Behavior

After reset:

- The controller shall be in the uninitialized state.
- The initialization-complete indication shall be deasserted.
- The error output shall indicate no error.
- Both effective access locks, read and write, shall indicate locked.
- The controller shall ignore bus read requests and shall not issue OTP commands until an initialization request is accepted.

The initialization request is only acted upon while the controller is uninitialized. Once the controller has initialized or entered a terminal error state, further initialization requests shall be ignored.

## 3. Initialization

An initialization request shall cause the controller to read the digest block from the end of its assigned OTP partition. During this read:

- The controller shall remain uninitialized.
- The partition shall remain locked.
- Bus read requests shall not be serviced.

When the OTP read response for the digest is received:

- If the response indicates no error, the controller shall capture the digest, assert the initialization-complete indication, and enter the idle state.
- If the response indicates a correctable ECC error, the controller shall still capture the digest and assert initialization-complete, but it shall report the correctable ECC error on the error output.
- If the response indicates any other OTP error, the controller shall not complete initialization. It shall record the OTP error and enter the terminal error state.

The controller does not compute the digest itself; it only reads and holds the digest value stored in the partition.

## 4. Effective Access Locking

The controller produces effective write-lock and read-lock statuses for the partition. These statuses determine whether accesses are permitted.

The effective write lock shall be locked when any of the following is true:

- The controller is not initialized.
- The incoming write-lock control indicates locked.
- If the partition is configured to use digest-based write locking, the held digest value is nonzero.

The effective read lock shall be locked when any of the following is true:

- The controller is not initialized.
- The incoming read-lock control indicates locked.
- If the partition is configured to use digest-based read locking, the held digest value is nonzero.

Incoming lock controls must propagate to the effective lock outputs. If an incoming lock is locked, the corresponding effective lock shall be locked.

An uninitialized partition shall always be locked for both read and write access, regardless of incoming lock controls or digest value.

## 5. Bus Read Transactions

When initialized, not in terminal error, and idle, the controller shall accept a bus read request.

At most one read transaction shall be outstanding at a time. While a read is being serviced, additional read requests shall not be accepted.

When a read request is accepted, the controller shall capture the requested address. It shall then check:

- Whether the byte address formed from the request is within the assigned partition range.
- Whether the effective read lock is unlocked.

If either check fails, the controller shall:

- Return a bus error response for that request.
- Report an access error on the error output.
- Not issue an OTP read.
- Return to the idle state.

This access error is non-terminal; the controller remains available for subsequent read requests.

If both checks pass, the controller shall issue a 32-bit OTP read request for the addressed word. When the OTP response is received:

- If the OTP response indicates no error, the controller shall return the 32-bit read data with a successful bus response.
- If the OTP response indicates a correctable ECC error, the controller shall still return the 32-bit read data with a successful bus response, and shall report the correctable ECC error on the error output.
- If the OTP response indicates any other error, the controller shall return a bus error response, report the OTP error on the error output, and enter the terminal error state.

## 6. OTP Interface Behavior

The controller is a read-only OTP master. Its behavior on the OTP interface shall be:

- It shall only issue OTP read commands.
- It shall present zero as write data.
- Before initialization completes, the only OTP request is the initialization digest read. The controller issues no OTP requests in the terminal error state.
- Digest reads shall use the full OTP block size for the digest.
- Data reads shall use the 32-bit word size.

The controller shall request the OTP word corresponding to the captured bus address. It shall not read data from outside the assigned partition range.

## 7. Error Reporting and Soft Error Handling

The error output shall represent the current error status of the controller.

A correctable ECC error from an OTP read shall be reported but shall not stop operation. This includes correctable errors received during initialization. The reported correctable error shall be cleared when the next bus read request is accepted.

An access error caused by an out-of-range or read-locked bus request shall be reported but shall not stop operation. It shall be cleared when the next bus read request is accepted.

## 8. Terminal Error State

The controller shall enter the terminal error state under any of the following conditions:

- An OTP read response returns an error other than no-error or correctable ECC error.
- The stored digest register detects an uncorrectable ECC error.
- The life-cycle escalation input is active.
- The controller detects an invalid internal operational state.

While in the terminal error state:

- The initialization-complete indication shall be deasserted.
- The effective read and write locks shall be locked.
- No new bus read requests shall be accepted.
- No OTP read requests shall be issued.
- The error output shall remain in the terminal error condition.
- The terminal error state shall be sticky until reset.

If the terminal error state is entered without a specific latched error, the controller shall report a generic FSM state error. If life-cycle escalation is asserted, the controller shall report the generic FSM state error unless a more specific error has already been latched.

A pending initialization or bus read transaction shall be abandoned if a terminal error condition occurs before the transaction completes.

## 9. Digest Output

The digest output shall be the digest value loaded during initialization. It shall remain stable while the controller is initialized and not in terminal error.

The digest storage is protected against corruption. If an uncorrectable ECC error is detected in the stored digest, the controller shall enter the terminal error state and report a check-fail type error.

## 10. Summary of Operational Modes

- **Uninitialized:** Waiting for initialization request. Partition is locked. No accesses are serviced.
- **Initializing:** Reading and validating the digest. Partition remains locked. No bus accesses are serviced.
- **Idle/read servicing:** Initialized and operational. Bus reads are serviced from OTP. Soft OTP errors may be reported without stopping operation.
- **Terminal error:** Partition is locked down. No bus or OTP activity occurs. The error status remains until reset.
